clue.text: Rude in a gentle fashion

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape or make it anew, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone is being rude, but in a gentle way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' reads as a noun ('in a gentle fashion' = gently) but is a verb telling you to rework IN A GENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude in the sense of crude or unrefined is a synonym for lacking grace and polish.

clue.text: She's a big noise in Tyne and Wear

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: Tyne and Wear is a county in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A woman who makes herself heard around Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big noise' suggests an important person, but means a loud racket. Tyne and Wear is an English county around Newcastle, in the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: 'She' stands for any woman, here a girl's name.

clue.text: An article to be followed

explanation.surface: A piece of writing that demands to be obeyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's editorial article is called its leading piece; and a person in front is someone others follow.

clue.text: One has no power in banking

explanation.surface: A person without influence in the world of finance.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpowered aircraft relies on air currents, and it banks (tilts) to turn in flight.

clue.text: Clear round called in this game for ladies

parts.note: net as an adjective means clear, after deductions (net profit)
something called round, a sphere, is a ball

explanation.surface: In a women's game someone shouts out a round score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' looks like a shout in the game but only names the round thing; 'in' is a link. NET means clear as in net income, after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport traditionally played by women and girls, scored by shooting into a ring.

clue.text: Too self-important to hit it back to us? Nothing in it

indicators.note: back tells us the word it is read backwards

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone too grand to bother returning a shot to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word it; 'in it' puts nothing (zero) inside us. The surface is a game where a shot is hit back.
explanation.definitionFit: Being puffed up and conceited is the same as being too full of one's own importance.

clue.text: Airmen ate in mess to refresh the body

indicators.note: a mess is a muddle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: RAF crew eat in the mess hall to restore themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the military dining room where airmen eat; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring back to life is to give the body new vigour, restoring it.

clue.text: Being in wrong groove and getting tied up in a knot causes depravity

indicators.note: wrong tells us the letters for groove are put out of order

parts.note: a rut is a groove worn in a track

indicators.note: something in a knot is tangled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Being stuck in the wrong rut and tangled up leads to moral decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns RUT into TUR; 'in a knot' rearranges TIED UP into PITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness or baseness of character is a synonym for moral corruption.

clue.text: Foreign office

explanation.surface: A government department dealing with other countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for a writing desk or agency comes from French, so is foreign; and it means an office or department.

clue.text: Those wanting the best offer views about a catalogue

indicators.note: about places the views around the following pieces

explanation.surface: Perfectionists put forward opinions on a published catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamers who pursue perfection are people aiming for the highest standard.

clue.text: Unwrap and start firing

explanation.surface: Taking the paper off a parcel, then starting to shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwrap a parcel is to make it uncovered; troops begin shooting when guns are made to fire.

clue.text: Where army authority is vested as a rule

explanation.surface: Military command usually lies with a senior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Command of an army rests with a senior officer; and the phrase means usually or on the whole.

clue.text: One's fate in Saudi Arabia?

parts.note: the word for destiny comes from Arabic and Turkish, so is how an Arab might name a person's lot

explanation.surface: Wondering what destiny awaits someone in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Destiny or one's lot in life, a loanword from Arabic via Turkish.

clue.text: Deadly weapons babies have

explanation.surface: Infants carrying lethal arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and rifles are guns carried by hand; and infants have little limbs.

clue.text: Driver's record vehicle scratched outside

indicators.note: outside puts the scratched word around the vehicle

parts.note: scored means scratched or marked with lines

explanation.surface: A motorist's log, kept by a car with scratches all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist, but it is a golfer: a golf driver is the club for long shots, and the round is written down on a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer notes the strokes per hole on a card, which is the player's record of a round.

clue.text: Once round garden that's in submission

indicators.note: round puts the word once around the following pieces

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A garden once handed in for judging.
explanation.definitionFit: Submitting to authority is yielding to it, which is the same as compliance.

clue.text: Smart little creature

explanation.surface: A clever little animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is British slang for sharp-witted; and an insect is a small creature.

clue.text: Charge costs nothing-not right

indicators.note: not says the letter for right is dropped

explanation.surface: A charge that costs nothing is not fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a payment demanded for a service, a charge.

clue.text: Animal Kay brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom, so the name is reversed

explanation.surface: A pet raised by a girl named Kay.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-haired ox of Tibet is an animal.

clue.text: Grim Scotsman and sailor about

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scotsman
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A gloomy Scot with a seafaring friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome and ghastly things are grim.

clue.text: A condition little Edward ended up with

parts.note: but introduces a condition or objection
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A requirement that young Edward finished up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To border on something is to have one's end meeting it.

clue.text: Not all people feel kindly towards deer

indicators.note: not all says only part of the words people feel kindly is used

explanation.surface: Most people are fond of deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deer of northern forests, the moose.

clue.text: Lily supporting party banner

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour party

explanation.surface: A lily held up beneath a political party's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A labarum was Constantine's military standard, a banner bearing the Chi-Rho.

clue.text: Behold a revolutionary in a Texan town

indicators.note: in puts the article and revolutionary inside the word for behold

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Look at an insurgent in a Texas town.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on the Rio Grande in Texas, on the Mexican border.

clue.text: The union that speaks with one voice

explanation.surface: A trade union whose members all say the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A large British public-sector trade union; and the word means saying or singing together in agreement.

clue.text: Have a bet about ass, you dog

indicators.note: about puts the word bet around the animal

explanation.surface: Someone told they are a dog wagers on a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged hound with long ears is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Less than half are psychotic!

parts.note: the short slang form of a word for a psychotic sufferer is under half the length of the full medical word, and implies only some are

explanation.surface: A gloomy claim that a minority of people are mentally ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a statistic; really it says the slang word is a clipped form, less than half of the full word for the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang clipping of the clinical term, used loosely for someone mentally unstable.

clue.text: There are many at the bakers' ball

definitions.text: There are many at the bakers' ball

parts.words: There are many at the bakers' ball
parts.note: read as a pun, a baker's party would be a dance of a round sweet roll; plainly it means a great quantity

explanation.surface: A crowded party held by the bakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty or a large quantity, punningly split into a sweet roll's dance.

clue.text: One who bowed to a papist woman

parts.note: RC, Roman Catholic, is a papist

explanation.surface: Someone bowing low to a Catholic lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowed' suggests bending at the waist; it means drawing a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots with a bow, so is a person who has bowed in that sense.

clue.text: Formal attire in which to treat hearts, say

parts.note: to dress a wound is to treat it
hearts is an example of a suit in cards

explanation.surface: Formal clothes worn to tend heart patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' suggests the organ; it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening clothes for men are formal wear.

clue.text: Mother takes a vehicle up for use by bandsman

indicators.note: up means read backwards, as the clue is across but this piece is turned around

explanation.surface: Mum borrows a car for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattle shaken in Latin music is an instrument a band member uses.

clue.text: Derivation of English mother-race

parts.note: a nation is a race or people

explanation.surface: Tracing a word's origins in an English motherland people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something issuing or flowing from a source is a derivation.
